items.title: 'They have even handed guns to children': What Iranians say is happening on their streets
items.description: Iran has been handing out guns to children as young as 12, as Donald Trump threatens a ground invasion. Here's what people in Iran are feeling.

items.title: Live: US and Iran race to find missing aviator as Trump threatens 'Hell' if deal not reached
items.description: Donald Trump gives Iran 48 hours to make a deal before "all Hell will reign down on them", as the US and Iran race to find a missing American aviator. Follow live.

items.title: Stagflation is already happening, a leading economist warns
items.description: With stagflation risks rising, what lessons could the treasurer learn from the past?

items.title: The quiet crisis unfolding inside Australia's universities
items.description: A generation ago studying in Australia opened doors. Today rising costs and falling satisfaction are making international students think twice, and locals feel sidelined.

items.title: Trash or treasure? Albanese's big gamble
items.description: Labor's landslide re-election brought renewed hope of reform, but in the past 12 months many anti-gambling advocates only became further disillusioned.

items.title: Motorists urged to dob in service stations over fuel price hikes
items.description: The NSW government fast-tracks a compliance blitz to strengthen fuel price transparency and protect motorists from misleading pricing.

items.title: Police look for missing cocaine after ocean 'drop-off' during 'bizarre' journey
items.description: Setting off from Panama just before Christmas, police say the MV Raider started its journey towards Sydney with almost 6 tonnes of cocaine aboard worth nearly $2 billion.

items.title: Queen at 100 is honoured in fashion exhibition as Andrew scandal bites
items.description: Within palace walls the Queen was a godlike figure. As her glorious fashion goes on display to commemorate what would have been her 100th birthday, how would she have responded to the Andrew crisis if alive today?

items.title: Whole villages in Sumatra erased overnight — and still living in the wreckage
items.description: Months after floods killed more than a thousand people across Sumatra, residents are still digging their way out of the wreckage. While survivors are eager to rebuild, many just can’t shake the fear that the next catastrophe is just around the corner.

items.title: After NT spent 'ridiculous' millions on aircraft, operations move offshore
items.description: A modern version of a 1960s-era aircraft that can land on sea and snow was meant to be built in NSW, and then in the NT. But years later it still hasn’t taken off.

items.title: The 'mudcrabs' battling to remediate Sydney's sickest waterway
items.description: Scurrying about the banks of Sydney's Cooks River, an army of volunteers known as the 'mudcrabs' is working to bring one of the nation's most toxic waterways back to life.

items.title: Artemis crew enter day four with plans to take manual control of spacecraft
items.description: The Artemis astronauts have been taking a moment to look back at Earth as they continue deep into space toward the Moon.

items.title: 'Doesn't make any sense': Young Aussies can't justify fuel costs to get to work
items.description: Young people are taking extraordinary steps to deal with the fuel crisis, including cutting back on work because the cost of fuel to get there is now higher than the money they will earn for the shift.

items.title: Too young for social media, but old enough to be locked up
items.description: As a nation, we have decided that a teenager cannot navigate a social media algorithm, but a 10-year-old can navigate a courtroom. For Australia's 2025 UN youth representative Satara Uthayakumaran, the contradiction is impossible to ignore.

items.title: Aerial photographer's hunt for 'Easter eggs' yields stunning images
items.description: Scott McCook spends his spare time photographing the salt lakes of WA's Wheatbelt, which look uncannily like giant eggs when viewed from the air.

items.title: I don't have all day to watch you struggle at an internet quiz
items.description: It's painfully obvious you're going to fail this quiz, so let's get it over with and return to our Sunday mornings, shall we?

items.title: Thom Yorke's solo tour was one of a kind. This Aussie film captured it
items.description: The award-winning Australian team behind a new concert film of the Radiohead frontman's debut solo tour discusses how it happened and why it matters.

items.title: Albany woman smashes WA's record for heaviest pumpkin with 408kg feat
items.description: A pumpkin grown in Albany has beaten the previous WA record for heaviest pumpkin by nearly 60 kilograms.

items.title: Two arrested as part of investigation into movements of Dezi Freeman
items.description: Two people have been arrested as police investigate the movements of Dezi Freeman, who was fatally shot by police last week after months on the run.

items.title: Australian helps Oxford end women's Boat Race drought
items.description: Competing for Oxford in the historic women's Boat Race for a fourth time, Australia's Annie Anezakis finally tastes victory.

items.title: Regurgitated citrus and a 'nearly dislocated' shoulder: Lisa Millar takes on Gayndah
items.description: The big cities may have their Easter shows and Ekkas, but Lisa Millar was reminded why nothing beats the small-town festival while filming the latest episode of Back Roads in Gayndah.

items.title: 'Chock-a-block' cemetery means non-Catholics have no grave options
items.description: The Anglican church in a small northern Tasmanian town has exhausted all its cemetery space after selling off land to accommodate new social and affordable housing.

items.title: Three dead, two critical in spate of crashes on Queensland roads
items.description: The state's road toll for 2026 is at least 80, compared to 59 by April 1 last year.

items.title: Brazilian admits to 'fan-girling' during win over Gilmore at Bells Beach
items.description: Luana Silva is overwhelmed to defeat one of her idols, Australia's eight-time world champion Stephanie Gilmore, in the first round.

items.title: 'Amazing' breakthrough as rare bird relearns its lost 'love song'
items.description: There are only about 250 regent honeyeaters left in the wild, and they have been losing their unique call, mimicking other birds instead. Conservationists say they are now successfully teaching young birds their traditional song.
